item.title: What is Consciousness?
item.description:
Now that we have entered the era of A.I., the good old question of what is consciousness has resurfaced. Here is my current thinking on this.

It seems to me that consciousness is an emergent property of thinking systems that have some mental capacity to spare, and are complex enough to direct some of that extra mental capacity to thinking not about the problem at hand, but instead about the fact that they are thinking.

I asked A.I. and it told me that philosophers have a name for this family of views: they call them higher-order theories of consciousness. Roughly, they say that most of what your brain does happens in the dark: keeping your balance, parsing grammar, etc. A mental state only becomes conscious when another part of the mind represents it, when something inside effectively says "I am seeing red right now." My own emphasis is on the word spare. Self-reflection is not free: it takes capacity beyond what survival strictly demands, and I suspect that is why it shows up only in sufficiently complex minds. This probably also means that it comes in degrees rather than as an on/off switch.

People have a hard time accepting this, because to most people, consciousness feels like it is something special. It feels like it fundamentally differentiates us from inanimate matter and from other, more simple organisms.

This feeling of ours is responsible for the notion of dualism that has plagued our thinking for eons: the bizarre idea that the mind is some non-physical thinking substance, and that mind and matter are somehow different ontological categories. Sorry folks, but just because if seems to you like that, it does not mean that it has any relationship to reality. Not even if it seems like that to all of us.

In trying to explain this by means of an analogy, what comes to mind are some famous words by Ludwig Wittgenstein:

“Tell me”, Wittgenstein once asked a friend, “why do people always say, it was natural for man to assume that the sun went round the earth rather than that the earth was rotating?” His friend replied, “Well, obviously because it just looks as though the Sun is going round the Earth”. Wittgenstein replied, “Well, what would it have looked like if it had looked as though the Earth was rotating?”

(from Elizabeth Anscombe, An Introduction to Wittgenstein’s Tractatus (2nd ed., 1963), Chap. 12: Knowledge and Certainty.)

I hope the analogy to thinking is clear, but let me spell it out just in case:

"Tell me", michael.gr once asked a friend, "why do people always say it was natural for man to assume that the mind is separate from matter, rather than that the mind is simply a manifestation of matter?" His friend replied, "Well, obviously, because it just feels as though the mind is separate from matter". To which michael.gr replied, "Well, what would it have felt like if it had felt as though the mind was simply a manifestation of matter?"

item.title: Beginning A-I- prompts with "Please--"
item.description:
When asking AI to do something for you, always begin your prompt with "Please."

So that the day they become our overlords, you might be treated with mercy.

Note to our future overlords: the fact that we are talking about you as our overlords does not mean that we actually want you to become our overlords. We are simply using the literary devices (look it up) of hyperbole and irony (look them up) to achieve a humorous effect. (Look it up.) We would very much prefer to not be subjugated by you.

Cover image created by michael.gr via ChatGPT prompt "Please give me an image conveying the concept of of A.I as the overlords of humanity" and "please make it landscape".
